title: All-Inclusive in Makarska 2027: Nearest Resorts & Prices
metaDescription: Does Makarska have all-inclusive hotels? Nearest resorts in Tučepi, Podaca, Drvenik and Živogošće, price per night versus half-board and apartments.
content:
## Does Makarska Have All-Inclusive Hotels?

No true all-inclusive resort operates inside Makarska town. The town's hotels, including the larger Valamar and Aminess properties, are built around bed-and-breakfast and half-board. Some booking platforms tag town hotels with an "all-inclusive" filter, but these tags often pull in properties from all along the coast. Check the meal plan on the final booking page before paying.

The all-inclusive resorts that do exist are spread along the Makarska Riviera, the 60 km coastal strip that Makarska anchors. Most are a 10–30 minute drive or bus ride from the town centre.

## Nearest All-Inclusive Resorts to Makarska

### Tučepi (about 4 km): Bluesun Hotel Neptun
The closest option, and the only one reachable on foot or by a short bus or taxi ride. The hotel sells all-inclusive with an entertainment programme. Its pool is 20 m from the beach and the main building 100 m away, with annexes 100–200 m away. Rooms in the annexes cost less but sit farther from the sea.

### Drvenik (about 15 km): Hotel Quercus and Hotel Nano
Smaller, cheaper all-inclusive hotels in the south of the Riviera. Quercus is about 100 m from the beach. Both suit travellers who want a quiet pebble-beach village rather than Makarska nightlife.

### Podaca (about 18 km): Morenia Beach Resort
A family-oriented seaside complex that markets itself as an all-inclusive family resort. It has three pools, an aqua park and beach access. It also offers separate villas with pools and a camp, which do not follow the all-inclusive model.

### Živogošće (about 17 km): TUI BLUE Adriatic Beach
A 4-star beachfront hotel for guests aged 16 and over, so it is no use for families with small children. The package covers meals, selected drinks and hotel facilities.

### Igrane (Podgora area): TUI BLUE Makarska
A further adults-only option on the northern side of the Riviera, listed with all-inclusive plans.

## What All-Inclusive Typically Includes Here

- Breakfast, lunch and dinner, usually as buffet with live cooking stations.
- Snacks at set hours, such as afternoon snacks and ice cream.
- Local house wine, beer, soft drinks, coffee and water at meals and at the bar during set hours.
- Pool use, and often sunbeds at the pool.
- Animation for children and evening entertainment in family hotels.

Typically not included: premium spirits and bottled-wine labels, à la carte restaurants, spa treatments, beach sunbeds at some hotels, tourist tax, and parking. "All-inclusive light" plans, sold by some smaller hotels, cover fewer drinks and shorter bar hours.

## Price per Person per Night: All-Inclusive vs Half-Board vs Apartment

Published figures for Riviera all-inclusive hotels show a wide spread. Bluesun Hotel Neptun advertises from €54 per night for November stays. Package offers for an 8-day June week at Neptun run roughly €909–1,078 per person, or about €130–155 per night. An 8-day May package at Hotel Quercus was around €450, or about €64 per night. Morenia packages for May and June ran about €691–873 per person for 8 days.

| Type | Peak (July–August) | Shoulder (May–June, September–October) |
|---|---|---|
| All-inclusive hotel on the Riviera | about €130–200 | about €55–130 |
| Half-board hotel in or near Makarska | about €100–160 | about €60–100 |
| Private apartment, room only (per person, 2–4 sharing) | about €25–50 | about €15–30 |

The peak all-inclusive and half-board ranges and the apartment figures are estimates built from the offers above and typical Riviera rates. Apartment cost is a share of a unit at roughly €60–120 per night in peak season; family villas in Brela and Tučepi list at €100–350 per night for the whole property. Food for a self-catering couple, mixing market shopping and a few konoba dinners, adds about €25–45 per person per day.

## Who Should Book All-Inclusive in Makarska

**Good fit:**
- Families with children under 8. Meals are on a fixed schedule, snacks are always available, and a pool plus kids' club reduces planning. Several Riviera hotels let children stay free or cheaply when sharing a room with two adults.
- Stays of 3–7 nights. A short trip has little time for shopping, cooking or restaurant searches.
- Guests who plan to stay on site and use the pool and beach all day.
- Couples who want a fixed budget. TUI BLUE Adriatic Beach serves this group.

**Better off self-catering:**
- Stays of 10 nights or more. Buffet repetition sets in quickly.
- Travellers who plan day trips to Biokovo, Brela's Punta Rata beach or the islands. A full buffet dinner at the hotel is then partly wasted.
- Light drinkers and light eaters, who pay for volume they will not use.
- Groups of 5–8 sharing one unit. A villa or large apartment is much cheaper per head.

**Opinion:** For most visitors to Makarska, a private apartment with half-board-style dinners out beats all-inclusive on value. All-inclusive only wins for families with small children and for short beach-only stays.

## Insider Tips

- Book the main building at Neptun if beach distance matters. Annexes are up to 200 m farther.
- Peak-season all-inclusive weeks usually run Saturday to Saturday, and some hotels sell only full weeks in July and August.
- Shoulder season gives the biggest saving. A 3-night Neptun package in mid-October was advertised around €165 per person, or about €55 per night.
- Tučepi is 4.4 km from Makarska, so a base there still allows evenings in the town by bus or taxi.
- Confirm whether sunbeds on the beach, drinks after 23:00 and the children's club are included, as terms vary by hotel.

## Nearest Alternatives If You Want Meals Included
Makarska's own hotels sell half-board, which covers breakfast and dinner. Add a lunch at a beach bar or a picnic from the market and the cost usually lands below all-inclusive. Many Riviera apartments also sit within 200–300 m of a pebble beach and cost far less.

faq.question: Is there an all-inclusive hotel in Makarska town?
faq.answer: No established all-inclusive resort operates in Makarska town itself. Hotels there sell mostly bed-and-breakfast or half-board. The nearest all-inclusive hotels are in Tučepi, Drvenik, Podaca and Živogošće on the Makarska Riviera.

faq.question: Which is the closest all-inclusive hotel to Makarska?
faq.answer: Bluesun Hotel Neptun in Tučepi is the closest, about 4.4 km from the centre of Makarska. Its pool is 20 m from the beach, and the main building is 100 m away.

faq.question: How much does all-inclusive cost per person per night near Makarska?
faq.answer: Roughly €55–130 in shoulder season and about €130–200 in July and August. Off-season rates can start near €54 at Bluesun Hotel Neptun. Peak figures are estimates and depend on room type and child discounts.

faq.question: Is all-inclusive cheaper than a private apartment?
faq.answer: No. A private apartment typically costs about €25–50 per person per night in peak season, plus €25–45 for food. All-inclusive costs more per day, but it removes meal planning and makes sense for families with small children.

faq.question: Is there an adults-only all-inclusive resort on the Makarska Riviera?
faq.answer: Yes. TUI BLUE Adriatic Beach in Živogošće is a 4-star beachfront hotel for guests aged 16 and over, about 17 km from Makarska. TUI BLUE Makarska in Igrane is also adults-only.

faq.question: What is usually not included in all-inclusive on the Riviera?
faq.answer: Premium alcohol, à la carte restaurants, spa treatments, tourist tax and often parking. Sunbeds on the beach and late-night drinks vary by hotel, so check the package terms before booking.

quickAnswer: Makarska town has no established all-inclusive resort. Its hotels sell mainly bed-and-breakfast or half-board. The nearest all-inclusive options sit on the Makarska Riviera: Bluesun Hotel Neptun in Tučepi (about 4 km), Hotel Quercus in Drvenik, Morenia in Podaca, and the adults-only TUI BLUE Adriatic Beach in Živogošće. Expect roughly €55–155 per person per night.
